heading: Think Reverse: Find the Safe Cells
body:
Instead of finding surrounded regions, **flip the logic**: mark which `'O'`s are safe (border-connected).

- Start DFS from all **border** `'O'`s
- Mark reachable `'O'`s as `'S'` (safe)
- Any unmarked `'O'` → surrounded → flip to `'X'`

heading: Why Border Cells Are the Key
body:
Any `'O'` reachable from a border `'O'` cannot be surrounded — it has a path to the edge.

**Gotcha:** Don't start DFS from interior cells. Only border `'O'`s guarantee safety.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we start DFS from border cells instead of searching for surrounded regions directly?
options: Because border-connected 'O's are safe by definition, making unmarked 'O's surrounded
Because DFS only works when starting from edges of a grid
Because it reduces time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)
Because we need to check all cells exactly once
explain: Border-connected 'O's can't be surrounded—they reach the edge. Reverse logic is simpler than detecting enclosure directly.
